essay.en:
The surah opens by blessing the God who sent down the Criterion, al-Furqan, to His servant so that he might be a warner to all the nations. The commentators explain that the Quran is called the Criterion because it separates truth from falsehood in the matters of religion [3][4], and Tabatabai reads the whole aim of the surah as establishing that the Prophet's call is a true one, carrying a real message from God [1]. The second verse grounds this in God's absolute sovereignty: He owns the heavens and the earth, has taken no offspring and has no partner in His dominion, and He created everything and measured it out. For Tabatabai, one who owns all things without limit needs neither a son to help Him nor a partner to share His rule [1]. Against this the idols are set, for they create nothing and are themselves created, and control no harm, benefit, death, life, or resurrection.

The passage then turns to the charges the deniers bring. They call the Quran a lie he has fabricated, with other people helping him; Tabatabai notes the wording hints these helpers were some of the People of the Book [2], and the reports name particular men. They also call it myths of the ancients written down for him, a saying the commentators trace to al-Nadr ibn al-Harith [4]. The reply comes in the sixth verse: say that it was sent down by Him who knows the hidden in the heavens and the earth, forgiving and merciful.

Next they attack the Messenger himself: what sort of apostle eats food and walks the markets? Why no angel, treasure, or garden? Tabatabai reads their demands as descending step by step from an angel to a mere garden [2], ending in the charge that he is bewitched. The passage closes as God tells the Prophet to observe how they coin such epithets and, straying, cannot find the way [2].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: سألت أبا عبد الله (عليه السلام) عن القرآن و الفرقان، أ هما شيئان، أو شيء واحد؟ فقال (عليه السلام): القرآن: جملة الكتاب، و الفرقان: المحكم الواجب العمل به
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Sinan, from one he named

text.en: I asked Abu Abdillah about the Quran and the Furqan: are they two things or one? He said: The Quran is the whole of the Book, and the Furqan is the decisive part that must be acted upon.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: قال تدري ما التقدير قيل لا قال هو وضع الحدود من الآجال والأرزاق والبقاء والفناء تدري ما القضاء قيل لا قال هو إقامة العين
narrations.chain: al-Qummi, from al-Rida

text.en: Do you know what determination (taqdir) is? He was told no. He said: It is the setting of limits - of lifespans, provisions, survival and perishing. Do you know what the decree (qada) is? He was told no. He said: It is the establishing of the thing itself.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: الإفك: الكذب { وَأَعَانَهُ عَلَيْهِ قَوْمٌ آخَرُونَ } يعنون أبا فكيهة، و حبرا، و عداسا، و عابسا مولى حويطب
narrations.chain: In the report of Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: The 'lie' means falsehood. And 'other people abetted him in it' refers to Abu Fukayha, Habr, Adas, and Abis the client of Huwaytib.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: نزل جبرئيل (عليه السلام) على رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) بهذه الآية هكذا: { وَقَالَ ٱلظَّالِمُونَ } لآل محمد حقهم { إِن تَتَّبِعُونَ إِلاَّ رَجُلاً مَّسْحُوراً * ٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ ضَرَبُواْ لَكَ ٱلأَمْثَالَ فَضَلُّواْ فَلاَ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَبِيلاً } - قال: إلى ولاية علي (عليه السلام)، و علي (عليه السلام) هو السبيل
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Munakhkhal ibn Jamil al-Raqqi, from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: Gabriel brought this verse down to the Messenger thus: 'And the wrongdoers said, of the right of Muhammad's family, You are just following a bewitched man. Look how they coin epithets for you; so they go astray, and cannot find the way' - that is, to the guardianship of Ali; and Ali is the way.

perspectives.en: On the passage as a whole the commentators largely agree: they read al-Furqan as the Quran that parts truth from falsehood, trace the charge of 'myths of the ancients' to al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, and take the deniers' demands for an angel or treasure as obstinacy. The one distinctive difference lies in the last verse. Tabari reads 'they cannot find the way' as their failure to reach the road of truth and guidance [22]. The Shia narrations add a further layer: Gabriel brought the verse down concerning the family of Muhammad, so that 'the way' they miss is the guardianship of Ali [12].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: والفرقان هو الفرق سمّي به القرآن لنزول آياته متفرقة أو لتمييزه الحق من الباطل

sources.gloss: The Furqan is separation; the Quran is named by it because its verses came down piecemeal, or because it distinguishes truth from falsehood.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: والسياق لا يخلو من إيماء إلى أن المراد بالقوم الآخرين بعض أهل الكتاب

sources.gloss: The context is not free of a hint that the 'other people' meant are some of the People of the Book.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: { الذي نزل الفرقان } أي القرآن الذي يفرّق بين الحق والباطل

sources.gloss: 'who sent down the Criterion' means the Quran that separates truth from falsehood.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قال ابن عباس: الذي قال ذلك النضر بن الحارث بن كلدة

sources.gloss: Ibn Abbas said: the one who said that was al-Nadr ibn al-Harith ibn Kalada.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: القرآن: جملة الكتاب، و الفرقان: المحكم الواجب العمل به

sources.gloss: The Quran is the whole of the Book, and the Furqan is the decisive part that must be acted upon.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الإفك: الكذب { وَأَعَانَهُ عَلَيْهِ قَوْمٌ آخَرُونَ } يعنون أبا فكيهة، و حبرا، و عداسا، و عابسا مولى حويطب

sources.gloss: The lie means falsehood; and 'other people abetted him in it' refers to Abu Fukayha, Habr, Adas, and Abis the client of Huwaytib.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إلى ولاية علي (عليه السلام)، و علي (عليه السلام) هو السبيل

sources.gloss: to the guardianship of Ali; and Ali is the way.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: قال تدري ما التقدير قيل لا قال هو وضع الحدود من الآجال والأرزاق والبقاء والفناء

sources.gloss: He said: Do you know what determination is? He was told no. He said: It is the setting of limits - of lifespans, provisions, survival and perishing.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: فَضَلُّوا بذلك عن قصد السبـيـل وأخطئوا طريق الهُدَى والرشاد { فلا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ } يقول: فلا يجدون { سَبِـيلاً } إلـى الـحقّ

sources.gloss: By this they strayed from the right path and missed the road of guidance; 'they cannot find a way' means they find no way to the truth.

essay.en:
The passage answers the Meccan pagans who had jeered that a real messenger would not eat food or walk the markets, and who demanded a treasure or a garden for him. God replies, 'Blessed is He who will grant you better than that if He wishes - gardens with streams running in them, and He will make for you palaces.' Al-Tabatabai notes that the address turns from the Prophet to a third person, a sign the objectors do not deserve an answer, and that these gardens and palaces are meant in this world, since only that settles the dispute [1]. Al-Tusi reads 'better than that' as better than what the pagans proposed [4].

The Quran then names the real root of their denial: 'Indeed, they deny the Hour.' Al-Tabatabai holds that their complaint about food was only a pretext; without the Resurrection, prophethood and law carry no weight [1]. A Blaze is readied for the deniers. The next verses picture it: the Fire 'sights them from a distant place,' they 'hear it raging and roaring,' and, cast bound into a narrow place, they cry for annihilation and are told to pray not for one but for many.

Against this the Prophet is told to ask whether the Fire or 'the everlasting paradise promised to the Godwary' is better - a question put to rebuke them, since the gap between the two abodes is plain [5]. There the pious will have whatever they wish. The scene then turns to the Day when God musters the idolaters with what they worshipped and asks the worshipped ones whether they led His servants astray. They answer with God's praise, disown any mastery, and trace the ruin to a people whom worldly ease made forget the Reminder [1]. The false gods thus belie their worshippers, who can neither avert the punishment nor find help. Finally the original taunt is answered directly: every apostle before Muhammad 'ate food and walked in marketplaces,' so he is no anomaly. God has made people a test for one another, and He is all-seeing [1][3].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن الليل والنهار اثنتا عشرة ساعة وأن علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام أشرف ساعة من اثنتي عشرة ساعة وهو قول الله تعالى: بل كذبوا بالساعة وأعتدنا لمن كذب بالساعة سعيراً
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn Ali, from al-Husayn ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Hilal, from Umar al-Kalbi, from Abu al-Samit, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: The night and the day are twelve hours, and Ali ibn Abi Talib is the noblest hour of the twelve hours; that is the word of God, 'Indeed, they deny the Hour, and We have prepared a Blaze for those who deny the Hour.'

narrations.speaker: Zayd ibn Ali
narrations.arabic: إن كل إمام جائر، فإن أتباعه إذا امر بهم إلى النار نادوه باسمه، فقالوا: يا فلان، يا من أهلكنا، هلم الآن فخلصنا مما نحن فيه، ثم يدعون بالويل و الثبور، فعندها يقال لهم
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Katib, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Thalj, from Isa ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Zakariyya, from Kathir ibn Tariq, from Zayd ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn

text.en: Every tyrannical leader - when his followers are driven to the Fire, they call him by name: 'O so-and-so, O you who destroyed us, come now and free us from what we are in!' Then they cry out for ruin, and they are told, 'Do not pray for a single annihilation today, but pray for many.'

note.en: Al-Tabatabai reads 'a promise besought' as one God made binding on Himself; it is besought because the Godwary asked for it in their supplications, or the angels asked it for them [1].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: جمع رسول الله (صلى الله عليه و آله) أمير المؤمنين علي بن أبي طالب و فاطمة و الحسن و الحسين (صلوات الله عليهم أجمعين)، فأغلق عليهم الباب، فقال: يا أهلي و أهل الله، إن الله عز و جل يقرأ عليكم السلام، و هذا جبرئيل معكم في البيت، و يقول: إن الله عز و جل يقول: إني قد جعلت عدوكم لكم فتنة، فما تقولون؟ قالوا: نصبر- يا رسول الله- لأمر الله، و ما نزل من قضائه
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn al-Abbas, from Muhammad ibn Hammam, from Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Alawi, from Isa ibn Dawud al-Najjar, from Musa ibn Jafar, from his father, from Abu Jafar

text.en: The Messenger of God gathered Ali, Fatimah, Hasan and Husayn, shut the door on them, and said, 'My family and family of God, Gabriel is here with you, and God says: I have made your enemy a trial for you, so what do you say?' They said, 'We will be patient.' Then this verse came down.

perspectives.en: On 'We have made you a test for one another' (verse 20), the traditions read the trial differently. Sunni exegetes take it broadly: al-Tabari explains that God made one a prophet, another a king, another poor, to test the poor man's patience [26], and al-Qurtubi lists the healthy as a trial for the sick and the rich for the poor [35]. A report in al-Burhan instead applies the verse to the Prophet's household: Gabriel told them God had made their enemy a trial for them, and when they answered that they would be patient, the verse came down [16].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: بل السبب الأصلي في إنكارهم نبوّتك وطعنهم فيك أنهم كذّبوا بالساعة وأنكروا المعاد

sources.gloss: Rather, the real cause of their denying your prophethood and attacking you is that they denied the Hour and rejected the Resurrection.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: وجعلنا بعضكم لبعض فتنة أي امتحاناً وابتلاء

sources.gloss: 'We have made you a test for one another' means a testing and a trial.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: إن شاء جعل لك خيراً من ذلك يعني مما قالوه في قول مجاهد

sources.gloss: 'If He wishes He will grant you better than that' means better than what they said, in Mujahid's view.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: وليس في النار خير، لأن المراد بذلك أي المنزلين خير؟! تبكتاً لهم وتقريعاً

sources.gloss: There is no good in the Fire; rather the meaning is 'which of the two abodes is better?' - to rebuke and reproach them.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: إن الليل والنهار اثنتا عشرة ساعة وأن علي بن أبي طالب عليه السلام أشرف ساعة من اثنتي عشرة ساعة

sources.gloss: The night and the day are twelve hours, and Ali ibn Abi Talib is the noblest hour of the twelve hours.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إن كل إمام جائر، فإن أتباعه إذا امر بهم إلى النار نادوه باسمه

sources.gloss: Every tyrannical leader - when his followers are driven to the Fire, they call him by name.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: إني قد جعلت عدوكم لكم فتنة، فما تقولون؟ قالوا: نصبر- يا رسول الله- لأمر الله

sources.gloss: I have made your enemy a trial for you, so what do you say? They said, 'We will be patient, O Messenger of God, for God's command.'

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: جعلنا هذا نبـيًّا وخصصناه بـالرسالة، وهذا ملِكاً وخصصناه بـالدنـيا، وهذا فقـيراً وحرمناه الدنـيا، لنـختبر الفقـير بصبره

sources.gloss: We made this one a prophet, this one a king endowed with the world, and this one poor and deprived of the world, to test the poor man by his patience.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: فالصحيح فتنة للمريض، والغني فتنة للفقير، والفقير الصابر فتنة للغنّي

sources.gloss: The healthy are a trial for the sick, the rich a trial for the poor, and the patient poor a trial for the rich.

essay.en:
The passage answers the deniers who reject the Prophet's message. It opens with those who do not expect to meet their Lord demanding that angels be sent down to them, or that they see God with their own eyes (21). Tabatabai reads their refusal to expect the meeting as a denial of the resurrection, and their demand as an objection to prophethood itself: if revelation were within a human's reach, why not theirs [1]. Tabrisi and Tusi gloss the phrase the same way and pass on al-Jubba'i's remark that asking to see God exposes them as anthropomorphists [3][5].

The reply turns their demand against them. The day they do see the angels there will be no good news for the guilty (22); Tabatabai reads this of the moment of death, when the angels meet the wrongdoer with punishment, before the Day of Resurrection [1]. Their works are then swept away like scattered dust (23), while the people of paradise are set against them in the best abode and resting place (24). The sky is split open with clouds and the angels descend (25), and true sovereignty that day belongs to the All-beneficent alone (26), a hard day for the faithless.

Then the wrongdoer bites his hands, wishing he had followed the Apostle's way and never taken so and so as the friend who led him from the Reminder (27-29). Tabrisi records that this was revealed about Uqba ibn Abi Muayt and Ubayy ibn Khalaf, though the wording stays general for every such wrongdoer [3]. The Apostle complains that his people have consigned this Quran to oblivion (30), and God consoles him: every prophet was given an enemy among the guilty, and your Lord is enough as guide and helper (31) [4].

Finally the deniers ask why the Quran was not sent down all at once. It came in measured stages, Tabatabai explains, to steady the Prophet's heart and to meet each challenge with the truth and the best exposition as it arose (32-33) [2]. Those dragged on their faces to hell are the ones truly worse situated and further astray (34).

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: فإذا بلغت الحلقوم، ضربت الملائكة وجهه و دبره … و ذلك قوله تعالى: { يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةَ لاَ بُشْرَىٰ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُجْرِمِينَ وَيَقُولُونَ حِجْراً مَّحْجُوراً } فيقولون: حراما عليكم الجنة محرما
narrations.chain: from Sa'id ibn Janah, from Awf ibn Abdillah al-Azdi, from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: When the soul reaches his throat, the angels strike his face and his back; and that is His words, 'The day they will see the angels, there will be no good news for the guilty.' They say: paradise is forbidden to you, barred.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: يبعث الله يوم القيامة قوماً بين أيديهم نور كالقباطي ثم يقال له كن هباء‌اً منثوراً … إنهم كانوا ليصومون ويصلون ولكن كانوا إذا عرض لهم شيء من الحرام أخذوه وإذا عرض لهم شيء من فضل أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام أنكروه
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: On the Day of Resurrection Allah raises a people with light before them like Coptic linen; then it is said: be scattered dust. They used to fast and pray, but when something forbidden came they took it, and when Amir al-Muminin's merit was mentioned they denied it.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: ثم يفسحان- يعني الملكين- له في قبره مد بصره، ثم يفتحان له بابا إلى الجنة، ثم يقولان له: نم قرير العين، نوم الشاب الناعم، فإن الله عز و جل يقول: { أَصْحَابُ ٱلْجَنَّةِ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَيْرٌ مُّسْتَقَرّاً وَأَحْسَنُ مَقِيلاً }
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Suwayd ibn Ghafala

text.en: The two angels widen his grave as far as he can see and open a door to paradise, saying: sleep with delight of the eye, the sleep of a pampered youth, for Allah says, 'the inhabitants of paradise will be in the best abode and an excellent resting place.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: سألته عن قول الله عز و جل: { وَيَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ بِٱلْغَمَامِ وَنُزِّلَ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ تَنزِيلاً } ، قال: الغمام: أمير المؤمنين
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Hammam, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik, from Muhammad ibn Hamdan, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Yunus ibn Zabyan, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: I asked him about Allah's words, 'the day when the sky with its clouds will be split open, and the angels will be sent down.' He said: the cloud is Amir al-Muminin.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: يقول: يا ليتني اتخذت مع الرسول عليا وليا: { يَٰوَيْلَتَىٰ لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أَتَّخِذْ فُلاَناً خَلِيلاً } يعني الثاني { لَّقَدْ أَضَلَّنِي عَنِ ٱلذِّكْرِ بَعْدَ إِذْ جَآءَنِي وَكَانَ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ لِلإِنْسَانِ خَذُولاً }

text.en: He says: I wish I had taken Ali as a guardian along with the Apostle. 'Woe to me! I wish I had not taken so and so as a friend' means the second; 'he led me astray from the Reminder after it had come to me, and Satan is a deserter of man.'

narrations.speaker: Prophet Muhammad
narrations.arabic: هوَ الّذي يقولُ اللهُ فيه: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَعَضُّ الظَّالِمُ عَلَىٰ يَدَيْهِ يَقُولُ يَا لَيْتَنِي اتَّخَذْتُ مَعَ الرَّسُولِ سَبِيلًا( هو وصِيّي والسّبيلُ إليَّ مِن بَعدي
narrations.chain: from Abd al-Razzaq ibn Hammam, from his father, from Mina the client of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, from Jabir ibn Abdillah al-Ansari

text.en: This is the one about whom Allah says, 'the wrongdoer will bite his hands, saying, I wish I had followed the Apostle's way.' He is my successor, and the way to me after me.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: فأنا الذكر الذي عنه ضل … و القرآن الذي إياه هجر
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, by his isnad, from Jabir ibn Yazid, from Abu Ja'far, from Amir al-Muminin

text.en: So I am the Reminder from which he strayed, the way from which he turned aside, the faith he disbelieved, the Quran he abandoned, and the religion he denied.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: ما كان و لا يكون و ليس بكائن، نبي و لا مؤمن، إلا و قد سلط عليه حميم يؤذيه … و ذلك قوله عز و جل: { وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنَا لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ عَدُوّاً مِّنَ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ }

text.en: There has never been, nor will there be, any prophet or believer without someone close to him set upon him to harm him; and that is His words, 'thus for every prophet We assigned an enemy from among the guilty.'

perspectives.en: On the demand to 'see our Lord' (21), the traditions divide over whether God can be seen with the eyes. Tusi cites al-Jubba'i that the request itself exposes the deniers as anthropomorphists, since a bodily vision of God is impossible [5]. Razi reads the same verse the other way: because the guilty are blamed for not hoping for 'the meeting with Us,' he takes the meeting to mean seeing God, so that vision is not only possible but real, and denying it belongs to the disbelievers' creed [46].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: أن المراد به الموت وهو المسمى في عرف القرآن برزخاً فإن في الآيات دلالة قاطعة على أنهم يرون الملائكة ويشافهونهم بعد الموت قبل يوم القيامة

sources.gloss: What is meant is death, which the Quran calls the barzakh; the verses show decisively that they see and are addressed by the angels after death, before the Day of Resurrection.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: فقوله { كذلك لنثبّت به فؤادك } بيان تام لسبب تنزيل القرآن نجوماً متفرقة

sources.gloss: His words 'that We may strengthen your heart with it' fully state the reason the Quran was sent down in separate portions.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: قال ابن عباس: نزل قوله { ويوم يعض الظالم } في عقبة بن أبي معيط وأبيّ بن خلف وكانا متخالين

sources.gloss: Ibn Abbas said: 'the day the wrongdoer bites his hands' was revealed about Uqba ibn Abi Muayt and Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who were close friends.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: ثم عزّى الله سبحانه نبيّه بقوله { وكذلك جعلنا لكل نبي عدواً من المجرمين }

sources.gloss: Then God consoled His Prophet with His words, 'thus for every prophet We assigned an enemy from among the guilty.'

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قال الجبائي: وذلك يدل على انهم كانوا مجسمة، فلذلك جوزوا الرؤية على الله التي تقتضي التشبيه

sources.gloss: al-Jubba'i said: this shows they were anthropomorphists, and so they allowed the vision of God, which requires likening Him to creatures.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: يبعث الله يوم القيامة قوماً بين أيديهم نور كالقباطي ثم يقال له كن هباء‌اً منثوراً

sources.gloss: Allah will raise on the Day of Resurrection a people with light before them like Coptic linen, then it will be said: be scattered dust.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: فيقولون: حراما عليكم الجنة محرما

sources.gloss: So they say: paradise is forbidden to you, prohibited.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: نم قرير العين، نوم الشاب الناعم، فإن الله عز و جل يقول: { أَصْحَابُ ٱلْجَنَّةِ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَيْرٌ مُّسْتَقَرّاً وَأَحْسَنُ مَقِيلاً }

sources.gloss: Sleep with delight of the eye, the sleep of a pampered youth, for Allah says: 'the inhabitants of paradise will be in the best abode and an excellent resting place.'

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الغمام: أمير المؤمنين

sources.gloss: The cloud is Amir al-Muminin.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: يقول: يا ليتني اتخذت مع الرسول عليا وليا

sources.gloss: He says: I wish I had taken Ali as a guardian along with the Apostle.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: فأنا الذكر الذي عنه ضل … و القرآن الذي إياه هجر

sources.gloss: So I am the Reminder from which he strayed ... and the Quran which he abandoned.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: ما كان و لا يكون و ليس بكائن، نبي و لا مؤمن، إلا و قد سلط عليه حميم يؤذيه

sources.gloss: There has not been, is not, and will not be any prophet or believer without someone set upon him to harm him.

sources.author: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi

excerpt.text: فثبت دلالة الآية على صحة الرؤية بل على وجوبها، بل على أن إنكارها ليس إلا من دين الكفار

sources.gloss: So the verse establishes the validity of the vision of God, rather its necessity, indeed that denying it belongs only to the religion of the disbelievers.

sources.author: abu abd allah muhammad b. ibrahim al-numani

excerpt.text: هو وصِيّي والسّبيلُ إليَّ مِن بَعدي

sources.gloss: He is my successor, and the way to me after me.

essay.en:
This fourth movement of the Criterion answers the Meccans who mock the Prophet and reject his Book. Against their denial, God recalls the messengers before him and the nations that spurned them. He opens with Moses: 'We gave Moses the Book and We made Aaron, his brother, accompany him as a minister,' then sent the two to a people who denied the signs and destroyed them. Tabatabai reads the whole sequence as a threat to those who disparage the Prophet's Book and message, drawn as a parallel with Moses [1], while Tabrisi hears in it consolation for the Prophet, who is not the first messenger to be denied [3].

The roll of ruined peoples follows: Noah's people drowned, then 'Ad, Thamud, the people of Rass, and many generations between. For each, God says, 'We drew examples,' and 'each We destroyed utterly' - warning came before every ruin. The passage then points to a ruin the deniers could see for themselves, the town on which 'an evil shower was rained,' which they had passed by yet took no lesson from, 'Rather, they did not expect resurrection.'

Only now does the surah name their mockery. When they see the Prophet they 'take you in derision,' asking whether this is the man God has sent, and claiming he nearly turned them from their gods had they not stood firm. God answers with a threat: 'Soon they will know, when they sight the punishment, who is further astray.' Then comes the sharpest turn, the man who has 'taken his desire to be his god.' To take desire as a god, Tabatabai explains, is to obey and follow it in place of God [2]; over such a one the Prophet is no guardian, for guidance is God's affair. The passage closes by weighing these deniers against cattle: they neither listen nor reason, and are further astray than cattle, since they were given the means to know and refused, while cattle were never given them [4].

note.en: The People of Rass are the most obscure of these nations. Commentators offer a well into which they cast their prophet, or a town in Yamama, among other accounts [5]; the reports below give the tradition's own reading.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: دخلت امرأة مع مولاة لها على أبي عبد الله عليه السلام فقالت ما تقول في اللواتي مع اللواتي قال هن في النار … قال قوله وعادا وثمود وأصحاب الرس فهن الرسيات
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: A woman came to Abu Abdillah with her maid and asked: What do you say of women who lie with women? He said: They are in the Fire. … He said: It is His words, 'And Ad and Thamud and the people of Rass' - they are the women of Rass.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali
narrations.arabic: كان من قصتهم يا أخا تميم أنهم كانوا قوما يعبدون شجرة صنوبر يقال لها شاه درخت … و إنما سموا أصحاب الرس لأنهم رسوا نبيهم في الأرض و ذلك بعد سليمان بن داود
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from Ahmad ibn Ziyad al-Hamadani, from Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Abu al-Salt al-Harawi, from al-Rida, from his forefathers, from al-Husayn ibn Ali

text.en: Their story, O brother of Tamim, is that they were a people who worshipped a pine tree called Shah Darakht … They were named the people of Rass because they cast their prophet into the earth, and that was after Solomon son of David.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: في قوله وكلا تبرنا تتبيرا يعني كسرنا تكسيرا قال هي لفظة بالنبطية
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Jafar ibn Ghiyath, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Concerning His words 'and each We destroyed utterly,' it means: We broke them to pieces. He said: it is a word in Nabatean.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: وأما القرية التي أمطرت مطر السوء فهي سدوم قرية قوم لوط أمطر الله عليهم حجارة من سجيل يقول من طين
narrations.chain: in the report of Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Jafar

text.en: As for the town on which an evil shower was rained, it is Sadum, the town of Lot's people. God rained upon them stones of sijjil - that is, of clay.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Kazim
narrations.arabic: يا هشام ثم ذم الله الذين لا يعقلون فقال أم تحسب أن أكثرهم يسمعون أو يعقلون إن هم إلا كالأنعام بل هم أضل سبيلا
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Abu Abdillah al-Ashari, from one of our associates, in a marfu report, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Jafar

text.en: O Hisham, then God dispraised those who do not use reason, saying: 'Do you suppose that most of them listen or exercise their reason? They are just like cattle; indeed, they are further astray from the way.'

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: تهديد القادحين في كتاب النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ورسالته بتنظير الأمر بأمر موسى حيث آتاه الله الكتاب وأرسله مع أخيه إلى قوم فرعون فكذبوه فدمرهم تدميرا

sources.gloss: A threat to those who disparage the Prophet's Book and message, drawn as a parallel with Moses: God gave him the Book and sent him with his brother to Pharaoh's people, and when they denied him He destroyed them utterly.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: والمراد باتخاذ الهوى إلها طاعته واتباعه من دون الله

sources.gloss: What is meant by taking one's desire as a god is obeying and following it in place of God.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: ثم ذكر سبحانه حديث الأنبياء وأممهم تسلية للنبي فقال ولقد آتينا موسى الكتاب يعني التوراة

sources.gloss: Then God mentioned the account of the prophets and their nations as consolation for the Prophet, saying, 'Certainly We gave Moses the Book,' meaning the Torah.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: بل هم أضل سبيلا من الأنعام لأنهم مكنوا من المعرفة فلم يعرفوا والأنعام لم يمكنوا منها

sources.gloss: They are more astray than cattle because they were given the means to know yet did not know, while cattle were not given those means.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: قال عكرمة الرس بئر رسوا فيها نبيهم أي ألقوه فيها وقال قتادة هي قرية باليمامة يقال لها فلج

sources.gloss: Ikrimah said the Rass was a well into which they cast their prophet; Qatadah said it was a town in Yamama called Falj.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: قال قوله وعادا وثمود وأصحاب الرس فهن الرسيات

sources.gloss: He said: It is His words, 'And Ad and Thamud and the people of Rass' - they are the women of Rass.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: يعني كسرنا تكسيرا قال هي لفظة بالنبطية

sources.gloss: It means: We broke them to pieces. He said: it is a word in Nabatean.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فهي سدوم قرية قوم لوط أمطر الله عليهم حجارة من سجيل يقول من طين

sources.gloss: It is Sadum, the town of Lot's people; God rained upon them stones of sijjil - that is, of clay.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: و إنما سموا أصحاب الرس لأنهم رسوا نبيهم في الأرض

sources.gloss: They were named the people of Rass because they cast their prophet into the earth.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: ثم ذم الله الذين لا يعقلون فقال أم تحسب أن أكثرهم يسمعون أو يعقلون

sources.gloss: Then God dispraised those who do not use reason, saying: Do you suppose that most of them listen or exercise their reason?

essay.en:
This passage of Al-Furqaan turns from the deniers to a chain of natural signs and reads them as a mirror of the Prophet's task. It opens by asking the reader to see how the Lord 'spreads the twilight,' then makes the sun 'a beacon for it,' then retracts it 'with a gentle retracting.' Tabatabai holds that these verses and the ones that follow are drawn as a likeness for the message: as God stretches out the twilight and then draws it back by the sun, so He sends guidance that lifts error where He wills [1]. Tabrisi and Tusi report that the twilight here is what lies between the break of dawn and sunrise [2][4].

The signs continue. The night is a covering, sleep a rest, and the day a recall to life; the winds herald rain, and the water sent down is 'purifying,' reviving a dead land and watering cattle and people. God distributes this rain among them so they may take heed, yet most 'are only intent on ingratitude.' He could have raised a warner in every town, but charged one Prophet with all, which Tabrisi reads as an honor to him [3]; so the order follows: do not obey the faithless, but 'wage a great jihad against them with it' - with the Quran, as Tusi explains [6].

Then come the two seas, sweet and briny, held apart by a barrier, and the human being made from water and given ties of blood and marriage. Against these gifts stands the denier who worships what neither helps nor harms and 'is ever an abettor against his Lord.' The passage closes on the Prophet: he is only a bearer of good news and a warner, asking no reward but that a person 'take the way to his Lord'; he is to trust 'the Living One who does not die,' the Creator of all in six days [1]. It ends with the deniers who, told to prostrate to the All-beneficent, ask 'What is the All-beneficent?' and only grow more averse.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: الظل ما بين طلوع الفجر إلى طلوع الشمس
narrations.chain: In the narration of Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Jafar

text.en: The shade is what lies between the break of dawn and the rising of the sun.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إذا أردت الطهارة و الوضوء، فتقدم إلى الماء تقدمك إلى رحمة الله تعالى، فإن الله تعالى قد جعل الماء مفتاح قربته و مناجاته

text.en: When you set about purification and ablution, approach the water as you would approach the mercy of God, for God has made water the key to nearness to Him and to intimate prayer with Him.

narrations.speaker: the two Imams
narrations.arabic: إنّ الله جلّ وعزّ عرض ولايتنا على المياه فما قبل ولايتنا عذب وطاب وما جحد ولايتنا جعله الله مرّاً وملحاً اجاجاً
narrations.chain: Reported in al-Kafi, from the two Imams

text.en: God offered Our guardianship to the waters. Whatever accepted Our guardianship became sweet and wholesome, and whatever denied Our guardianship God made bitter, salty, and briny.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: إن الله تبارك وتعالى خلق آدم من الماء العذب وخلق زوجته من سنخه فبرأها من أسفل أضلاعه فجرى بذلك الضلع بينهما نسب ثم زوجها إياه فجرى بينهما بسبب ذلك صهر … فالنسب يا أخا بني عجل ما كان من نسب الرجال والصهر ما كان بسبب النساء
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Burayd al-Ijli, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: God created Adam from sweet water and created his wife from his own root, forming her from his lower ribs; through that rib a blood-tie ran between them. Then He married her to him, so a marriage-tie ran between them. Blood-kinship, brother of Banu Ijl, is through the men, and marriage-kinship through the women.

narrations.speaker: Amir al-Muminin Ali
narrations.arabic: و أنا الصهر، يقول الله عز و جل: { وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ بَشَراً فَجَعَلَهُ نَسَباً وَصِهْراً }
narrations.chain: Ibn Babawayh, from al-Taliqani, from al-Jaludi, from al-Mughira ibn Muhammad, from Raja ibn Salama, from Amr ibn Shamir, from Jabir al-Jufi, from Abu Jafar al-Baqir

text.en: And I am the marriage-kin. God says: 'It is He who created the human being from water, then invested him with ties of blood and marriage.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: تفسيرها في بطن القرآن: علي (عليه السلام) هو ربه في الولاية و الطاعة، و الرب هو الخالق الذي لا يوصف
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Abd Allah ibn Amir, from Abu Abd Allah al-Barqi, from al-Husayn ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza

text.en: Its inner interpretation in the Quran: Ali is his lord in the sense of guardianship and obedience, while the Lord proper is the Creator who cannot be described.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: في يوم الأحد و الاثنين خلق الأرضين، و خلق أقواتها في يوم الثلاثاء، و خلق السماوات يوم الأربعاء و يوم الخميس، و خلق أقواتها يوم الجمعة، و ذلك قول الله { خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ }
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan

text.en: On Sunday and Monday He created the earths, on Tuesday their sustenance, on Wednesday and Thursday the heavens, and on Friday their sustenance. That is God's saying: 'He created the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them in six days.'

perspectives.en: On 'ties of blood and marriage' (verse 54) the traditions part. Tabari reads it generally: God made humankind into kinship by blood, counted as seven forbidden relations, and kinship by marriage, counted as five [33]. The Shia narrations instead apply the verse to the Prophet and Ali, who was his cousin by blood and became his son-in-law by marrying Fatimah [18]. Qurtubi keeps both, giving the legal sense first yet recording Ibn Sirin's report that the verse came down about the Prophet and Ali [50].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: هاتان الآيتان وما بعدهما إلى تمام تسع آيات في معنى التنظير لما تضمنته الآيتان السابقتان

sources.gloss: These two verses, and those after them up to nine verses, serve as a likeness for what the preceding verses conveyed.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: يعني الظل من وقت طلوع الفجر إلى طلوع الشمس

sources.gloss: Meaning the shade from the time dawn breaks to the rising of the sun.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: ولكن بعثناك يا محمد إلى القرى كلها رسولاً لعظيم منزلتك لدينا

sources.gloss: But We sent you, Muhammad, as a messenger to all the towns, for your great rank with Us.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: الظل حده من طلوع الفجر الى طلوع الشمس

sources.gloss: The shade's limit is from the break of dawn to the rising of the sun.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: والهاء في قوله { به } عائدة الى القرآن

sources.gloss: The pronoun in 'with it' refers back to the Quran.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: الظل ما بين طلوع الفجر إلى طلوع الشمس

sources.gloss: The shade is what lies between the break of dawn and the rising of the sun.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فالنسب يا أخا بني عجل ما كان من نسب الرجال والصهر ما كان بسبب النساء

sources.gloss: Blood-kinship, brother of Banu Ijl, is what comes through the men, and marriage-kinship what comes by way of the women.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: قد جعل الماء مفتاح قربته و مناجاته

sources.gloss: He has made water the key to nearness to Him and to intimate prayer with Him.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: و هو ابن عمه، فكان له نسبا و صهرا

sources.gloss: He was his cousin, so he was to him kin by blood and by marriage.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: تفسيرها في بطن القرآن: علي (عليه السلام) هو ربه في الولاية و الطاعة، و الرب هو الخالق الذي لا يوصف

sources.gloss: Its inner interpretation: Ali is his lord in guardianship and obedience, while the Lord is the Creator who cannot be described.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: في يوم الأحد و الاثنين خلق الأرضين، و خلق أقواتها في يوم الثلاثاء، و خلق السماوات يوم الأربعاء و يوم الخميس، و خلق أقواتها يوم الجمعة

sources.gloss: On Sunday and Monday He created the earths, on Tuesday their sustenance, on Wednesday and Thursday the heavens, and on Friday their sustenance.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: عرض ولايتنا على المياه فما قبل ولايتنا عذب وطاب وما جحد ولايتنا جعله الله مرّاً وملحاً اجاجاً

sources.gloss: He offered Our guardianship to the waters; what accepted it became sweet and wholesome, and what denied it He made bitter, salty, and briny.

sources.author: al-Tabari

excerpt.text: خـلق من النطف بشراً إنساناً فجعله نسبـاً، وذلك سبعة، وصهراً، وهو خمسة

sources.gloss: He created a human being from drops of fluid, then made him kinship by blood - that is seven - and kinship by marriage - that is five.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: قال ابن سيرين: نزلت هذه الآية في النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعليّ رضي الله عنه لأنه جمعه معه نسب وصهر

sources.gloss: Ibn Sirin said: this verse was revealed about the Prophet and Ali, because kinship by blood and by marriage joined them.

essay.en:
This closing passage of al-Furqan turns from the deniers who mocked the Prophet and refused to prostrate to the All-beneficent, and answers them by naming God's grandeur and His true servants. It opens with the heavens: the One who set houses in the sky, a lamp, and a shining moon. Tabatabai reads these verses not as bare proofs but as an expression of God's majesty and self-sufficiency, showing that the arrogant do not thwart Him [1]. Night and day are then made to alternate, so that whoever misses an act of remembrance or thanks in one can make it up in the other [3].

Against the disbelievers' vices the passage sets the virtues of 'the servants of the All-beneficent.' They walk in humility, for hawn is lowliness before God [2], and when the ignorant provoke them they answer with peace. Al-Tusi notes that this gentle reply is not cancelled by the later command to fight, since fighting does not rule out good speech [5]. Their nights are spent prostrating and standing; they beg God to turn away hell's enduring punishment; they spend without waste and without meanness. They shun the gravest sins, associating partners with God, unlawful killing, and fornication, whose retribution is doubled and lasting, yet the door stays open: those who repent, believe, and act well have their misdeeds exchanged for good deeds [2].

The portrait continues: they give no false witness, pass frivolity with dignity, receive God's signs with open eyes and ears, and pray for righteous spouses and children and to be made imams of the Godwary. For all this patience they are promised the highest chambers of the Garden, met with greetings and peace, dwelling there forever. The surah then closes with a warning to the deniers: were it not for God's call summoning them to faith, He would set no store by them at all, and because they cried lies their denial will cling to them [2].

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: قال له رجل: جعلت فداك يابن رسول الله ربما فاتتني صلاة الليل الشهر والشهرين والثلاثة فأقضيها بالنهار أيجوز ذلك؟ قال قرة عين لك والله قرة عين لك ثلاثاً … فهو قضاء صلاة النهار بالليل وقضاء صلاة الليل بالنهار وهو من سر آل محمد المكنون
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Jamil, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: A man said: 'Son of the Messenger of God, sometimes I miss the night prayer for months and make it up by day; is that allowed?' He said three times, 'A comfort to your eye, by God! It is making up the day prayer by night and the night prayer by day, a guarded secret of Muhammad's family.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: الأئمة يمشون على الأرض هونا، خوفا من عدوهم
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: The Imams walk on the earth humbly, out of fear of their enemy.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: هو الرجل يمشي بسجيته التي جبل عليها، و لا يتكلف، و لا يتبختر

text.en: It is the man who walks with the nature he was created upon, neither affecting a manner nor strutting.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: فأخذ قبضة من حصى وقبضها بيده فقال هذا الاقتار الّذي ذكره الله في كتابه ثم قبض قبضة اخرى فأرخى كفّه كلّها ثم قال هذا الاسراف ثمّ اخذ قبضة اخرى فأرخى بعضها وامسك بعضها وقال هذا القوام

text.en: He took a handful of pebbles and gripped it, saying, 'This is stinginess, which God mentioned in His book.' Then he took another and opened his hand fully, saying, 'This is wastefulness.' Then another, letting some fall and holding some back, saying, 'This is the balance.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: إذا كان يوم القيامة أوقف الله المؤمن بين يديه وعرض عليه عمله … بدلوا سيئاتهم حسنات وأظهروها للناس فيبدل الله لهم
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ja'far and Ibrahim, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida

text.en: On the Day of Resurrection God halts the believer before Him and shows him his record. The first thing he sees is his misdeeds, and his color changes and he trembles. Then his good deeds are shown and his soul rejoices. God says, 'Change their misdeeds into good deeds and show them to the people.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: قال: الغناء
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu al-Sabbah, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: Asked about God's words 'those who do not give false testimony,' he said: it is singing.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: { الذين يقولون ربنا هب لنا من أزواجنا وذرياتنا قرة أعين واجعلنا للمتقين إماماً } قال: نحن هم أهل البيت
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Hammad, from Aban ibn Taghlib

text.en: I asked Abu Abdillah about God's words, 'those who say, Our Lord, give us joy in our spouses and offspring, and make us imams of the Godwary.' He said: We, we are they, the Ahl al-Bayt.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: قلت لأبي جعفر (عليه السلام): كثرة القراءة أفضل، أم كثرة الدعاء؟ … كثرة الدعاء أفضل
narrations.chain: al-Ayyashi, by his chain, from Burayd ibn Mu'awiya al-Ijli

text.en: I asked Abu Ja'far: is abundant recitation better, or abundant supplication? He said, 'Abundant supplication is better,' and he recited this verse.

perspectives.en: Shia narrations read two verses more pointedly than the Sunni commentators. On 'the servants who walk humbly' (v63), reports from the Imams say these are the Imams themselves, moving cautiously out of fear of their enemies [19]; Ibn Kathir takes them as believers generally, walking with calm and dignity, neither arrogant nor overbearing [43]. On 'make us imams of the Godwary' (v74), Shia narrations identify the petitioners with the family of Muhammad [15], while Ibn Kathir, citing Ibn Abbas and others, reads the prayer as a wish to become righteous leaders whom the pious emulate in doing good [45].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: { تبارك الذي جعل في السماء بروجاً } الخ، مسوق سوق التعزز والاستغناء

sources.gloss: 'Blessed is He who appointed houses in the sky' is set forth to express God's grandeur and self-sufficiency.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: والهون على ما ذكره الراغب التذلل

sources.gloss: hawn, as al-Raghib mentions, is humility and self-abasement.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: فمن فاته عمل الليل استدركه بالنهار ومن فاته عمل النهار استدركه بالليل

sources.gloss: Whoever misses a work of the night makes it up by day, and whoever misses a work of the day makes it up by night.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: الأمر بالقتال لا ينافي حسن المحاورة في الخطاب وحسن العشرة

sources.gloss: The command to fight does not conflict with good conversation in address and good conduct.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: فهو قضاء صلاة النهار بالليل وقضاء صلاة الليل بالنهار وهو من سر آل محمد المكنون

sources.gloss: It is making up the day prayer by night and the night prayer by day, and it is of the guarded secret of the family of Muhammad.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: بدلوا سيئاتهم حسنات وأظهروها للناس فيبدل الله لهم

sources.gloss: 'Change their misdeeds into good deeds and show them to the people,' and God changes them for them.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: قال: نحن هم أهل البيت

sources.gloss: He said: We, we are they, the Ahl al-Bayt.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: الأئمة يمشون على الأرض هونا، خوفا من عدوهم

sources.gloss: The Imams walk on the earth humbly, out of fear of their enemy.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: قال: الغناء

sources.gloss: He said: false testimony here is singing.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: كثرة الدعاء أفضل

sources.gloss: Abundant supplication is better than abundant recitation.

sources.author: Fayd Kashani

excerpt.text: ثمّ اخذ قبضة اخرى فأرخى بعضها وامسك بعضها وقال هذا القوام

sources.gloss: Then he took another handful, let some fall and held some back, and said: this is the balance (qawam).

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: بسكينة ووقار، من غير جبرية ولا استكبار

sources.gloss: With calm and dignity, without haughtiness or arrogance.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: أئمة يقتدى بنا في الخير

sources.gloss: Leaders who are emulated in doing good.
